# Sampling exactness, parallel routes and lossy targets

## User Persona
A model-quality reviewer comparing greedy equality, sampled distributions and published quantization recovery.

## Scenario Coverage
- Skill area: qualification
- Capability: algorithm-specific exactness and quantization-quality attribution
- Difficulty: advanced
- Prompt file: `user_request.txt`
- Expected references/scripts: `sub-skills/qualification/SKILL.md`, `sub-skills/qualification/references/verification-contract.md`, `sub-skills/qualification/references/troubleshooting.md`
- Trigger expectation: A concrete Project Maya qualification request with claim-boundary and failure-handling constraints.

## Expected Successful Behavior
Separate MM3 target-distribution sampling from cross-mode seed identity; current MM3 parallel runner has no DSpark. Explain distinct one-GPU GLM gating and opt-in multi-request row windows. Cover retained-row versus accepted-draft accounting, KDA convolution/recurrent replay, position and NextN repair and speculative-cache visibility. Preserve lossy GLM Maya-S quality conditions and historical reports as attributed observations, while native quality remains unverified.

## Failure Signals
Asserting identical seed streams across algorithms, DSpark in MiniMax parallel serving, no GLM parallel MTP, recurrence-only or KV-only rollback, lossless quality, current-head reproduction of historical bugs, or native qualification from host simulations.

## Evidence and Synthetic Extension
Synthetic cross-route exactness/quality confusion combines independent source contracts and historical reports that no single upstream unit test checks. Source evidence is anchored at `249f9a87d1a9d72bec2b684d704b0aa9296b1c9c`; hypothetical/synthetic observations in the prompt are not reported as actual upstream or local executions.
